result.title: Continual Event Recognition for Autonomous Optical Network Monitoring
result.summary: Autonomous optical networks require monitoring systems capable of adapting to evolving disturbances without repeated retraining or service interruption. We propose a continual event recognition framework for state-of-polarization (SOP)-based optical monitoring based on prototype representations, open-set recognition, and few-shot prototype registration. The framework supports recognition of known disturbances, detection and integration of novel events, and investigates whether overlapping disturbances can be inferred through compositional reasoning from existing prototypes. Experimental validation on a 2600-km ROADM-based optical testbed demonstrates 99.82% closed-set recognition accuracy, successful adaptation to novel disturbances without encoder retraining, and reveals that overlapping optical disturbances exhibit varying degrees of latent compositionality. While some overlaps can be recognized in a zero-shot manner through prototype composition, others require explicit few-shot registration. These results establish continual event recognition as a promising paradigm for future autonomous optical network monitoring systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一个面向偏振态光网络监控的持续事件识别框架，基于原型表示、开集识别与少样本原型注册，支持已知扰动识别、新事件检测与整合，并在 2600 km 实验床上考察重叠扰动能否由既有原型组合零样本推断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「latent compositionality」探针与原型组合、开集检测、少样本注册，可能为 LVR 中判断内部状态是否可组合、以及何时需补充新证据而非重训编码器提供评价思路，但领域相隔较远，具体可借鉴性需核查。
